items.headline: Nvidia weighs playing the cosigner for Nscale’s AI data center in West Virginia
items.excerpt: When investors get nervous about AI spending, it helps to have the chipmaker that sells the chips offer to cosign the loan.

items.headline: Ollie, a privacy-focused AI assistant, is shutting down
items.excerpt: As an increasing number of AI assistants flood the market, the founder of Ollie, an assistant that respected its users' privacy, says it will be shutting down in a week.

items.headline: Intel’s stock crashes, knocking $12B from government’s stake
items.excerpt: Intel is being hurt by PC sales as the AI industry gobbles memory and other components causing PC prices to rise.

items.headline: Anthropic expected to receive high ‘junk’ rating from credit agencies following IPO, FT report says
items.excerpt: Blackstone's forecast is just a prediction, but naturally, a high junk rating would make it more difficult and costlier for Anthropic to raise the money to keep funding its massive spending that has undergirded its business.

items.headline: Last-minute Halloween costumes for tech nerds
items.excerpt: No Halloween costume? Just be a deceptively cute AI agent icon, a PHP vulnerability, or sleepy time Bryan Johnson.

items.headline: Cracks are emerging in the AI spending boom
items.excerpt: Big Tech is pouring billions into AI infrastructure, but mounting debt, negative cash flow, and growing investor skepticism are raising questions about the sustainability of the AI spending boom.

items.headline: Zest’s new AI agent finds restaurants and books reservations over text
items.excerpt: Can't agree on where to eat? Zest's AI concierge can combine everyone's tastes, put restaurant options to a vote, and make the reservation.

items.headline: Google’s first data center satellite is online and writing poetry
items.excerpt: The first TPU in space is running a Google DeepMind Gemma 4 model and writing cheesy poetry.

items.headline: Theranos whistleblower Tyler Shultz warns that the AI boom is ‘a great opportunity to go deceive people’
items.excerpt: The cautionary Theranos tale takes on a new significance in the AI era, when companies that have never turned a profit are raising capital at trillion-dollar valuations.

items.excerpt: At TechCrunch Founder Summit 2026, happening November 4 at SoWa Power Station in Boston, networking powered by Braindate is designed to make those conversations easier to find, whether they are in 1:1 or small-group on-site meetings. items.headline: DoorDash said it’s only received ‘several hundred’ orders from AI agents
items.excerpt: DoorDash said that it is open to working with third-party agent makers.

items.headline: 5 days left: Your last chance to connect, scale, and save at TechCrunch Founder Summit 2026
items.excerpt: 5 days to save up to $100, plus a second pass for free to TechCrunch Founder Summit 2026 in Boston on November 4. Register now.

items.headline: Can AI data centers be mass-produced like cars? This startup aims to find out
items.excerpt: Runware is building a factory to turn out prefabricated AI data centers on an assembly line. The real test will be whether it can deliver at that scale.

items.headline: You don’t need to believe in a god to get a religious exemption from using AI at work
items.excerpt: David Durman, a University of Kentucky administrator, recently earned a religious exemption from using AI in the workplace.

items.headline: AWS will be a $1T business, Jassy says — but first, it will spend big
items.excerpt: Amazon wants to be the king of AI cloud computing and become the first $1 trillion revenue business. But to do that it will have to continue on its capex spending spree, its CEO said Thursday.

items.headline: As search traffic dries up, Reddit announces it’s shifting to a logged-in experience
items.excerpt: As AI transforms how people find information online, Reddit is rethinking its open-web roots to protect its audience and business.

items.headline: Rivian expands joint venture with VW to include AI assistant
items.excerpt: Rivian doesn't disclose if the value of its $5.8 billion joint venture will expand as a result.

items.headline: OpenAI-backed Thrive Holdings acquires ADT
items.excerpt: OpenAI-backed Thrive Holdings is buying ADT in a $15.3 billion deal, with plans to bring AI to the home security business.

items.headline: Meta quietly launches an AI fashion app called Style Sketch
items.excerpt: The app connects to Instagram to build a virtual closet from photos you’ve already shared, or lets you add items manually by snapping a photo, recording a quick video, or uploading images from your camera roll.

items.headline: Granola crunches up a dictation feature to compete with Wispr
items.excerpt: Uno reverse! After Wispr added meeting notes to its dictation app, Granola is adding dictation to its meeting notetaker. The voice AI wars are getting interesting.
